title: The Quot presheaf is an algebraic space, locally finitely presented for finitely presented source
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $a:A\to B$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Assume that $a$ is separated and of finite presentation. Let $\mathcal F$ be any quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_A$-module, using the module conventions and the proper-support Quot presheaf of [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. There exist an algebraic space $R$ over $S$, a morphism $r:R\to B$, and bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_B(T,R)\simeq\operatorname{Quot}_{\mathcal F/A/B}(T)$ natural in all schemes $T\to B$. If $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_A$-module, then $r$ is locally of finite presentation. No flatness or properness of $a$ and no finite-presentation assumption on $\mathcal F$ are required for the representability assertion.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C=\mathcal C_{A/B}$ be the algebraic stack supplied by [lem-sfb-space-coherent-stack-general]; its hypotheses are exactly separatedness and finite presentation of $a$. Form a category fibred in groupoids $\mathcal Q$ whose objects over $T$ are $(b:T\to B,q:\mathcal F_T\twoheadrightarrow Q)$ with the target conditions of [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. An arrow over $v:T\to T_1$ is a pullback isomorphism $\alpha:v_A^*Q_1\simeq Q$ intertwining the quotients. The pullback transitions and their composition are those already specified by that definition; thus $\mathcal Q$ is fibred in groupoids. Forgetting the quotient map gives a morphism $j:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal C$. No stack assertion about $\mathcal Q$ has yet been used.

source.place: Tag 09TU, proposition-quot, first two paragraphs; quotient groupoid rather than its discrete skeleton.

proof.text: Fix an object $(b:T\to B,G)$ of $\mathcal C$. The base change $A_T\to T$ is finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], and $\mathcal F_T$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. Hence [lem-sfb-space-module-hom-affine] supplies an affine algebraic space $H/T$ for maps $\mathcal F_U\to G_U$. The 2-fibre product $T\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal Q$ is naturally equivalent to the discrete functor of surjections among these maps. Indeed its objects over $U/T$ are $(q:\mathcal F_U\twoheadrightarrow Q,\theta:Q\simeq G_U)$; send this to $\theta q$. The inverse sends $u$ to $(u,\mathrm{id})$. Between two such objects an arrow, if present, must be $\theta_2^{-1}\theta_1$, and it intertwines the quotients exactly when their composites with $\theta_i$ coincide. These formulas commute with pullback.

source.place: Tag 09TU, proposition-quot, description of the 2-fibre product and application of Tag 08K6.

proof.text: Let $H^{\mathrm{surj}}\subset H$ be this subfunctor. For every scheme $V\to H$, the Hom bijection of step 2 gives a module map $u:\mathcal F_V\to G_V$ on $A_V$. The morphism $A_V\to V$ is finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. The module $G_V$ is finitely presented, flat with proper support because it is the pullback family in $\mathcal C$ of [lem-sfb-space-coherent-stack-general]; finite presentation implies finite type by taking the images of the finitely many local free generators. Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-surjectivity-open] to $u$. It identifies $V\times_HH^{\mathrm{surj}}$ with an open subscheme of $V$ for arbitrary further base changes. Thus [def-a1-space-open-subspace] makes $H^{\mathrm{surj}}$ an algebraic space. Step 2 therefore proves that $j$ is representable by algebraic spaces. By [lem-sfb-stack-representable-source-algebraic], $\mathcal Q$ is algebraic.

source.place: Tag 09TU, proposition-quot, last paragraph (Tag 09TP and Tag 05UM); scheme tests avoid presupposing a universal map over a space.

proof.text: Every automorphism $\alpha$ of $(b,q)$ in $\mathcal Q(T)$ satisfies $\alpha q=q$. Since $q$ is a surjection of sheaves of modules, sections of its target locally lift, so $\alpha$ fixes every section locally and hence globally: $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-setoid-space] to obtain an algebraic space $R/S$ naturally equivalent to $\mathcal Q$. Its bijections identify $R(T)$ with pairs $(b,[q])$, where $[q]\in\operatorname{Quot}_{\mathcal F/A/B}(T,b)$ by [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Projection to $b$ gives a morphism $r:R\to B$. Taking the fibre at each fixed $b:T\to B$ gives the required relative bijections. They commute with all scheme morphisms because the equivalence, the class map and the projection use the pullback transitions.

source.place: Tag 09TU, proposition-quot, application of Tag 04SZ and passage from total to relative functors.

proof.text: Now suppose $\mathcal F$ is finitely presented. Its pullback $\mathcal F_T$ is finitely presented: tensoring a local presentation $\mathcal O^m\to\mathcal O^n\to\mathcal F\to0$ gives the same finite presentation after pullback, since $N\otimes(M/L)=(N\otimes M)/\operatorname{im}(N\otimes L)$. Thus [lem-sfb-space-module-hom-affine] makes $H\to T$ in step 2 finitely presented. The open immersion $H^{\mathrm{surj}}\to H$ of step 3 is locally finitely presented: on scheme charts principal opens have ring presentation $R[t]/(ft-1)$. Its composite to $T$ is locally finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Hence every scheme base change of $j$ is locally finitely presented. Choose a surjective etale scheme chart $V\to B$. The definition of the two groupoids identifies their base changes with $\mathcal Q_{A_V/V}$ and $\mathcal C_{A_V/V}$. The base-changed $a$ is separated and finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition, lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. The scheme-base clause of [lem-sfb-space-coherent-stack-general] makes $\mathcal C_{A_V/V}\to V$ locally finitely presented. Applying the local-finite-presentation clause of [lem-sfb-stack-representable-source-algebraic] over $V$ gives a smooth surjective scheme atlas $W\to\mathcal Q_{A_V/V}$ with $W\to V$ locally finitely presented. Through the equivalence $\mathcal Q_{A_V/V}\simeq h_{R\times_BV}$ of step 4, $W\to R\times_BV$ is smooth and surjective, and both $W\to R\times_BV$ and $R\times_BV\to V$ are representable by algebraic spaces; [lem-sfb-smooth-cover-flat-lfp-descent] therefore makes $R\times_BV\to V$ locally finitely presented on etale scheme charts. The chart criterion [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] therefore gives that $r$ is locally of finite presentation. All uses of finite presentation of $\mathcal F$ occur in this step.

source.place: Tag 09TU, local-finite-presentation conclusion, expanded via Tags 08K6, 08KD, 06CN and 06Q3. Smooth-source descent of local finite presentation: stacks-properties.tex Tag 06M2 with spaces-descent.tex Tag 06EV.

lean.statement: theorem exists_properQuot_representing_space {S : Scheme.{u}} {A B : AlgebraicSpace S} (a : A ⟶ B) (ha : ProperQuotFinitePresentation a) (hsep : MapIsSeparated a) (F : A.QCoh) : ∃ (R : AlgebraicSpace S) (r : R ⟶ B) (e : ∀ T : ProperQuotTest B, { f : yoneda.obj T.left ⟶ R.obj.obj // f ≫ r.hom.hom = T.hom } ≃ (properQuotFunctor a ha F).obj (op T)), (∀ (T' T : ProperQuotTest B) (h : T' ⟶ T) (f : { f : yoneda.obj T.left ⟶ R.obj.obj // f ≫ r.hom.hom = T.hom }) (f' : { f : yoneda.obj T'.left ⟶ R.obj.obj // f ≫ r.hom.hom = T'.hom }), yoneda.map h.left ≫ f.val = f'.val → e T' f' = (properQuotFunctor a ha F).map h.op (e T f)) ∧ (F.obj.IsFinitePresentation → MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation r)
